newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal competition body reports on tobacco sale.
newsitem.headline: Portugal competition body reports on tobacco sale.

text.p: Portugal's Competition Council should complete its review on Thursday of the proposed privatisation of state tobacco concern Tabaqueira-Empresa Industrial de Tabacos, a council official said on Wednesday.
But the official said that the Council would not make any direct comparisons between the bids of the three candidates for the 65 percent stake that the state wants to sell.

He told Reuters that the Council, whose opinion was sought by the Economy Ministry, would issue three separate reports on the competing consortiums led by Spain's Tabacalera, Philip Morris and French group Seita, respectively.

Tabacalera, which is flanked by Portugal's Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos made the highest offer at 36.47 billion escudos ($237 million). Philip Morris, which is allied to local group Jorge de Mello bid 33.2 billion, while Seita pitched its proposal at 31.2 billion.
But the government decision will also take account of development plans for the local tobacco industry and will not be based simply on price.
The economy ministry asked for a ruling from the Competition Council because of the virtual monopoly that Tabaqueira has in the domestic market.

"Tomorrow...the Council will take individual decisions for each of the three (potential) buyers," the official said, adding that the opinions would probably be sent to the ministry at the end of Thursday's meeting.
The government has said it is still optimistic that it will be able to carry out the proposed privatisation of Tabaqueira during 1996.
